subject: Archaeology
title: 3D Photogrammetry Underwater
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: 3D Photogrammetry Underwater.

hook.text: Thousands of overlapping photos can build a perfect 3D model of a shipwreck — freezing an entire site in digital time.

buildup.text: Divers or robots photograph every angle of a wreck. Software stitches the images into a centimeter-accurate 3D model.

discovery.text: Archaeologists can study a site remotely, zoom in on details, and share models with colleagues worldwide.

twist.text: The technique works on sites too deep or dangerous to revisit. Once scanned, the model outlasts the wreck itself.

climax.text: Public museums now display interactive 3D wreck models. Anyone with a browser can explore a Roman shipwreck from home.

punchline.text: You can now explore a 2,000-year-old shipwreck from your couch.

quiz.question: Why is 3D photogrammetry valuable for underwater archaeology?
options: It replaces the need for divers entirely
Digital models outlast the wreck and can be studied remotely by anyone
It can reveal artifacts hidden inside sealed containers

details.summary: Underwater photogrammetry uses overlapping photographs to create precise 3D digital models of submerged sites. This technique allows millimeter-accurate recording of shipwrecks and underwater structures, creating permanent digital archives that can be studied, shared, and revisited long after.
details.whyItMatters: Photogrammetry gives underwater sites the same recording precision as land archaeology. Digital 3D models preserve sites that may deteriorate, be looted, or become inaccessible, democratizing access to underwater heritage worldwide.
takeaways: Photogrammetry creates 3D models from overlapping photographs
It achieves millimeter-accurate recording of underwater sites
Digital archives preserve sites that may deteriorate over time

faq.question: How does underwater photogrammetry work?
faq.answer: Divers or ROVs take hundreds of overlapping photos from multiple angles. Software identifies matching points across images and calculates their 3D positions, generating dense point clouds that are converted into textured 3D models accurate to within millimeters.

faq.question: Why is 3D recording better than traditional drawings?
faq.answer: 3D models capture every visible detail simultaneously, can be measured and analyzed remotely, and preserve spatial relationships that 2D drawings simplify. They allow researchers worldwide to study the site virtually and make new observations without returning to the field.
